title: Do Language Models Use Their Depth Efficiently?
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Residual-stream and causal-intervention analysis of Llama 3.1, Qwen 3 and OLMo 2: second-half layers mostly refine the current-token distribution, computation depth does not grow with problem difficulty, and deeper models stretch the same computation over more layers.
key_contributions: Layer-contribution, layer-skipping and residual-erasure analyses showing a mid-network phase transition in Llama/Qwen/OLMo
Depth score showing no dependence of processing depth on problem difficulty or hop count
Cross-model linear maps showing deeper models stretch the same computation; exploratory evidence that MoEUT (shared layers) uses depth more

setup.model_sizes: Llama 3.1 70B (main), Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 3, OLMo 2; Qwen 2.5 1.5B and 14B for linear maps; 244M Transformer and MoEUT trained from scratch
setup.train_tokens_or_data: analysis of public checkpoints; DeepMind Math for the from-scratch MoEUT/Transformer study
setup.benchmarks: GSM8K (10 random examples by default), MATH, MQuAKE, DeepMind Math

claims.claim: Layers in the second half of the network contribute much less to the residual stream than those in the first half, with a sharp phase transition near the middle.
claims.evidence_quote: layers in the second half contribute much less than those in the first half, with a clear phase transition between the two halves.

claims.claim: Skipping second-half layers barely affects computations at future token positions, so these layers do not compute reusable sub-results; they refine the current prediction.
claims.evidence_quote: the second half of the network barely has any effect on future computations, except for some special layers at the very top of the network.

claims.claim: The depth of computation (depth score) does not increase with MATH difficulty level or the number of hops in MQuAKE questions.
claims.evidence_quote: The depth of computation the model performs is independent of the problem difficulty and the number of hops in the input problem.

claims.claim: Linear maps from Qwen 2.5 1.5B layers to Qwen 2.5 14B layers show a diagonal pattern: the deeper model is a stretched-out version of the shallow one rather than doing new computation.
claims.evidence_quote: This shows that the big model is more likely a “stretched out” version of the shallow model, rather than one that does entirely new computations.

claims.claim: A shared-layer model (MoEUT) trained from scratch on DeepMind Math uses more of its depth and in a more input-dependent way than a standard Transformer (exploratory, manual study).
claims.evidence_quote: MoEUT uses more of its depth, and its depth seems to be more input-dependent.

claims.claim: The authors argue that if fixed computation depth is caused by the pretraining objective, recurrent latent-thinking methods (they cite the recurrent-depth model, 2502.05171) are fundamentally flawed; if it is architectural, such methods may be the solution.
claims.evidence_quote: If the insensitivity of computation depth to input complexity is the consequence of the pretaining objective, such methods are fundamentally flawed.

numbers.what: number of Open LLM Leaderboard base models in depth-vs-performance regression
numbers.quote: briefly analyzes the role of model depth in shaping model performance, using a dataset of 132 base models on the Open LLM Leaderboard

numbers.what: significance of depth as predictor of leaderboard score
numbers.quote: Depth is a highly significant variable in this model (p < 0.0001).

numbers.what: default number of GSM8K examples for the main analyses
numbers.quote: Unless noted otherwise, the results are computed on 10 random examples from GSM8K [22].

numbers.what: MoEUT extrapolation accuracy on Mul/Div Multiple Longer, with vs without modeling the question
numbers.quote: MoEUT on the “Mul/Div Multiple Longer” split has an accuracy of 36% if modeling the question is enabled, and 63% if it is not.

numbers.what: standard Transformer extrapolation accuracy, with vs without modeling the question
numbers.quote: The difference for standard Transformers is less dramatic (41 vs. 48%).

numbers.what: size of from-scratch MoEUT and baseline models
numbers.quote: We use the 244M parameter baseline and MoEUT models from the paper [16], without modifications.

numbers.what: examples per difficulty level for depth score
numbers.quote: We measure the above metrics on 20 different random examples for each expected depth.

limitations: Case study on a few model families; the linear-map study uses a single model pair (Qwen 2.5 1.5B/14B); the MoEUT study is a manual inspection of individual models; main analyses use small example sets (10 GSM8K examples by default, 20 per difficulty level).
venue: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025).
survey_notes: Core motivation evidence for the survey's 'depth is under-used in stacked Transformers' argument. Directly discusses looped/recurrent-depth models: cites 2502.05171 as a latent-thinking method and states the open question of whether fixed depth is caused by objective or architecture. MoEUT evidence is exploratory (manual, 244M, regime unclear) and should not be cited as a controlled iso-param result. Agrees with 2512.14064 (no dynamic depth use; long-CoT does not raise effective depth) and 2602.05970 (functionally similar layers); partially contradicted by 2604.12426 (some adaptive depth use, clearer after finetuning). Competing explanation for late-layer ineffectiveness: Pre-LN variance growth (2502.05795). Note the paper itself (App. B) finds depth is still a significant predictor of leaderboard performance, while 2001.08361 reports depth/width shape has minimal effect on loss within a wide range.

title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (adaptive_depth_without_sharing); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: MoD caps the number of tokens processed per block with expert-choice top-k routing (others take the residual path), giving a static compute graph; at isoFLOP training budgets MoD matches or beats vanilla Transformers with fewer FLOPs per forward pass.
key_contributions: Expert-choice top-k routing around non-shared Transformer blocks with a fixed per-block token capacity (static graph)
isoFLOP analysis (6e18, 2e19, 1e20 FLOPs) showing MoD shifts the optimum to larger, faster-stepping models
Causal auxiliary loss / predictor so the non-causal top-k can be used in autoregressive sampling; MoDE combination with MoE

setup.baselines: isoFLOP-optimal vanilla Transformer; stochastic-routing MoD; MoE
setup.benchmarks: training log-probability / loss; held-out autoregressive evaluation on 256000 sequences (500M tokens)

claims.claim: At equal training FLOPs, an MoD transformer can improve the final log-probability objective by up to 1.5% over a vanilla transformer with equal wall-clock training time.
claims.evidence_quote: one can train an MoD transformer that improves upon vanilla transformers by as much as 1.5% on the final log probability training objective for equivalent training FLOPs (isoFLOP)

claims.claim: MoD models match isoFLOP-optimal baselines while needing a fraction of the FLOPs per forward pass and stepping faster during sampling.
claims.evidence_quote: These models match baseline performance for equivalent FLOPS and wall-clock times to train, but require a fraction of the FLOPs per forward pass, and can be upwards of 50% faster to step during post-training sampling.

claims.claim: The best configuration routes every other block with 12.5% capacity; learned routing is essential, stochastic routing is drastically worse.
claims.evidence_quote: We found that it is best to use 12.5% capacity blocks, every other block.

claims.claim: Learned routing is crucial: stochastic (Gaussian-sampled) top-k routing performs drastically worse than both the baseline and learned-routing MoD.
claims.evidence_quote: Learned routing is crucial, as MoD transformers that use stochastic routing

claims.claim: When adding FLOPs to an MoD model, adding depth is better than adding width.
claims.evidence_quote: Empirically, we find that it is better to add depth than to add width when adding FLOPs to the model.

claims.claim: Gains from MoD compound with Mixture-of-Experts (MoDE), and integrated no-op experts beat simply reducing expert capacity.
claims.evidence_quote: In figure 7 we present results showing that the performance improvments offered by MoD compound with those of MoE.

numbers.what: speedup of MoD model #3 at equal performance to isoFLOP-optimal baseline
numbers.quote: Notably, model #3 achieves equal performance to the isoFLOP optimal baseline but steps 66% faster, due to the relatively fewer FLOPs needed per forward pass.

numbers.what: best capacity: tokens processed vs routed around per block
numbers.quote: 256, or 12.5% of the sequence’s tokens are processed by self-attention and the subsequent MLP, while 1792 tokens, or 87.5% of the sequence’s tokens route around the block

numbers.what: isoFLOP budgets and model size range
numbers.quote: We used the 12.5% capacity MoD variant to perform an isoFLOP analysis for 6e18, 2e19, and 1e20 FLOPs, training models varying in size from 60M to 3B parameters.

numbers.what: effect of causal auxiliary routing loss on LM objective
numbers.quote: a simple auxiliary loss that empirically affects the primary language modeling objective by approximately 0.2 − 0.3%

numbers.what: accuracy of the causal top-k prediction task
numbers.quote: We provide empirical evidence that this is a relatively easy auxiliary task that quickly achieves 99% accuracy.

numbers.what: max log-prob improvement at isoFLOP
numbers.quote: one can train an MoD transformer that improves upon vanilla transformers by as much as 1.5% on the final log probability training objective

limitations: Results are reported as training loss / held-out log-probability only (no downstream task benchmarks); top-k routing is non-causal and requires an auxiliary loss or predictor for sampling; memory savings noted but not studied.
survey_notes: Canonical non-shared adaptive-depth baseline: compute varies per token by skipping distinct (unshared) blocks; parameters unchanged, KV for skipped tokens not produced at that block. Contrasts itself with early exit (a token can skip middle layers and still be attended later) and mentions shared-weight iteration (Universal Transformers) only in related work, with no comparison to looped models. Its expert-choice routing is the mechanism later reused for per-token recursion depth in Mixture-of-Recursions (2507.10524, in corpus; assigned to adaptive_depth). Regime is clean iso-train-FLOP but the metric is loss only. 'Better to add depth than width' supports the depth-axis thesis, in tension with 2001.08361 (depth/width shape has minimal effect within a wide range).

title: A Survey on Latent Reasoning
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (prior_surveys_and_positions); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Survey of latent reasoning organized into vertical (activation-based, incl. looped/Universal Transformers and Coconut-style feedback) and horizontal (hidden-state, linear-attention/TTT) recurrence, plus layer-specialization interpretability and diffusion models framed as infinite-depth reasoning.
key_contributions: Unified spatial/temporal formulation of latent CoT (activation-based vs hidden-state-based updates)
Taxonomy: vertical recurrence (loop/UT, hidden-state feedback, training-induced) vs horizontal recurrence (linear-state, gradient-state)
Sections on layer-specialization interpretability and diffusion/optimization views of 'infinite-depth' reasoning

claims.claim: The survey's top-level taxonomy splits latent CoT into vertical recurrence (expanding computational depth) and horizontal recurrence (expanding sequential capacity).
claims.evidence_quote: These categories can be broadly divided into two types: 1) vertical recurrence for expanding computational depth, and 2) horizontal recurrence for increasing sequential capacity.

claims.claim: Explicit CoT transmits about 15 bits per step while a 2560-d FP16 hidden state carries about 40,960 bits, a bandwidth gap of roughly three orders of magnitude (motivation for latent reasoning).
claims.evidence_quote: exchanges full 2560-dimensional FP16 hidden states (≈ 40, 960 bits each), revealing a ∼ 2.7 × 103 fold bandwidth gap between the two approaches.

claims.claim: Recent looped architectures (Recursive Transformer, AlgoFormer, recurrent-depth) have converged on a Prelude/Loop/Coda structure.
claims.evidence_quote: recent architectures like Recursive Transformer [2], AlgoFormer [29], and Recurrent-Depth [31] have converged on a three-stage Pre/Loop/Coda structure.

claims.claim: The survey reads a trend from complex adaptive halting (ACT) to simple fixed or convergence-based stopping, and concludes adaptive mechanisms may not be worth their overhead (an interpretive claim, not tested).
claims.evidence_quote: This evolution suggests that complex adaptive mechanisms may not justify their computational overhead in practice.

claims.claim: Training-induced recurrence (Coconut, CODI, CCoT, pause/filler tokens) is framed as complementary to architectural looping.
claims.evidence_quote: The relationship between these training-induced methods and architectural recurrence is complementary rather than competitive.

claims.claim: The survey explicitly does not compare methods empirically and notes most studies compare to non-reasoning baselines rather than to each other.
claims.evidence_quote: Furthermore, most studies compare their models to non-reasoning LLM baselines rather than to each other.

claims.claim: Diffusion language models are framed as 'spatial infinite-depth reasoning' via iterative parallel denoising with adjustable step counts.
claims.evidence_quote: Spatial infinite-depth reasoning is realized by diffusion models that begin with a fully masked or noisy draft of the entire output and iteratively denoise it in parallel

claims.claim: Gradient-state recurrent models (TTT, Titans, Atlas) are framed as trading sequence length for depth: each token is an optimizer step on a fast-weight layer.
claims.evidence_quote: processing a longer sequence is mathematically equivalent to running the same layer for more optimization iterations, thereby yielding greater reasoning depth without adding parameters.

numbers.what: bits per explicit CoT token vs per latent hidden state (survey estimate)
numbers.quote: Explicit reasoning transmits discrete tokens (≈ 15 bits each), whereas latent reasoning

limitations: No empirical comparison across methods (stated by the authors); Table 1 design summaries are coarse; trend claims about depth embeddings and halting are interpretive.
survey_notes: Prior survey closest to ours. Positions looped transformers as one branch ('vertical recurrence') of latent reasoning and Coconut as a bridge ('activation with explicit hidden-state feedback'); our survey should differentiate by (i) treating recurrent depth as its own scaling axis and (ii) auditing comparison regimes, which this survey explicitly does not do ('does not offer a direct empirical comparison'). Its assertion that 'recurrent models exhibit unprecedented extrapolation abilities' (Sec. 3.1.5) should be tempered with 2305.15042 (overparametrized implicit models do not gain from more test-time iterations). Framing diffusion as infinite-depth reasoning is contested by 2507.12549, which argues diffusion models cannot solve inherently serial problems. Note the survey's Table 1 summarizes recurrent-depth stopping as fixed-point/convergence and says depth embeddings were 'tried, dropped'; verify against 2502.05171 itself before reuse.

title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Coconut feeds the last hidden state back as the next input embedding (continuous thought) instead of decoding a token, trained with a curriculum that replaces CoT steps by latent thoughts; it beats no-CoT, trails CoT on GSM8k, and beats CoT on ProsQA.
key_contributions: Continuous-thought paradigm: last hidden state re-enters as the next input embedding between <bot>/<eot> markers
Multi-stage curriculum (from iCoT) replacing k CoT steps by k*c continuous thoughts; ProsQA planning dataset
Probing analysis showing latent thoughts hold several frontier nodes (BFS-like value estimates)

setup.model_sizes: pre-trained GPT-2 (main); Llama 3.2-3B and Llama 3-8B (App. C.2)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: GSM8k synthetic data from Deng et al. (385,620 train), ProntoQA (9,000), ProsQA (17,886)
setup.loops_train: c continuous thoughts per removed reasoning step: c=2 (GSM8k, up to 6 thoughts), c=1 (ProntoQA/ProsQA, 6 stages)
setup.loops_test: same number of thoughts as final training stage (padded to constant length)
setup.baselines: CoT, No-CoT, iCoT, Pause token; ablations w/o curriculum, w/o thought, pause as thought

claims.claim: With 6 continuous thoughts, Coconut reaches 34.1% on GSM8k vs 16.5% for no-CoT (same GPT-2 base), but stays below language CoT (42.9%).
claims.evidence_quote: by using 6 continuous thoughts, Coconut achieves 34.1% accuracy on GSM8k, which significantly outperforms No-CoT (16.5%).

claims.claim: Coconut does not surpass CoT on GSM8k but gives a better accuracy/generated-token trade-off.
claims.evidence_quote: Although Coconut does not surpass CoT on GSM8k, it offers a superior trade-off between reasoning efficiency and accuracy (Figure 8, I).

claims.claim: Continuous thoughts can encode multiple candidate next steps, yielding BFS-like latent search on planning-heavy logical tasks where Coconut outperforms CoT.
claims.evidence_quote: continuous thoughts can encode multiple alternative next steps, allowing the model to perform a breadth-first search (BFS) rather than committing prematurely to a single deterministic path as in CoT

claims.claim: Without the multi-stage language-CoT curriculum, Coconut is no better than no-CoT: latent reasoning still needs language supervision to learn.
claims.evidence_quote: we found the models trained this way do not perform any better than no-CoT

claims.claim: On Llama 3.2-3B and Llama 3-8B, Coconut gains over no-CoT are consistent but smaller than at GPT-2 scale.
claims.evidence_quote: We observe consistent performance gains across both Llama 3.2-3B and Llama 3-8B models compared to the no-CoT baseline, though these improvements are not as pronounced as those previously demonstrated

claims.claim: Training requires n+1 sequential forward passes for n latent thoughts, which limits parallelism; adding 3 thoughts per step at once causes loss spikes and instability.
claims.evidence_quote: adding three continuous thoughts at once – particularly during the final stage transition – leads to a sharp spike in training loss, causing instability.

numbers.what: GSM8k accuracy: Coconut (6 thoughts) vs No-CoT
numbers.quote: by using 6 continuous thoughts, Coconut achieves 34.1% accuracy on GSM8k, which significantly outperforms No-CoT (16.5%).

numbers.what: CoT row of Table 1 (GSM8k acc, tokens; ProntoQA acc, tokens; ProsQA acc, tokens)
GSM8k accuracy of Coconut, w/o curriculum, w/o thought, pause as thought (Table 1)
numbers.quote: Coconut (Ours) - w/o curriculum - w/o thought - pause as thought 34.1 ±1.5 14.4 ±0.8 21.6 ±0.5 24.1 ±0.7

numbers.what: GSM8k accuracy of No-CoT, iCoT, Pause Token (Table 1)
numbers.quote: No-CoT iCoT Pause Token 16.5 ±0.5 30.0∗ 16.4 ±1.8

numbers.what: ProsQA accuracy of Coconut, w/o curriculum, w/o thought, pause as thought (Table 1)
GSM8k accuracy no-CoT vs Coconut for Llama 3.2-3B and Llama 3-8B (Table 5)
numbers.quote: Llama 3.2-3B Llama 3-8B no-CoT Coconut (Ours) 26.0 42.2 31.7 43.6

numbers.what: inference time per test case in seconds, No-CoT/CoT/Coconut on GSM8k, ProntoQA, ProsQA (Table 4)

limitations: Needs language-CoT curriculum supervision (no gain without it); n+1 sequential forward passes in training hamper parallelism; instability when adding 3 thoughts per step; does not beat CoT on GSM8k; smaller gains at 3B/8B; main experiments on GPT-2.
survey_notes: Anchor of family (a). Mechanism is recurrence along the sequence axis: each continuous thought is a full L-layer pass whose top hidden state re-enters at the bottom, so k thoughts give k*L serial layers and add k KV-cache entries (memory grows with thoughts, unlike depth looping). The paper itself links this to effective depth ('the effective depth of the transformer increases because the generated outputs are looped back to the input', citing Feng et al. 2305.15408) and lists looped transformers and 2502.05171 as related or future integration targets, but runs no comparison against a looped model. Regime: all methods share the same pretrained GPT-2 (iso-param, same data) but use different numbers of inference passes (not iso-inference-FLOP). Superposition/BFS claim: theory support in 2505.12514 and 2509.23365; contested by 2604.06374, which finds superposition collapses or goes unused in fine-tuned regimes (Coconut finetunes a pretrained GPT-2). Successors that address its weaknesses: CODI (2502.21074, self-distillation), SIM-CoT (2509.20317, step supervision against collapse), PCCoT (2506.18582, Jacobi-parallel training), Soft Tokens (2509.19170, RL), PonderLM-2 (2509.23184, pretraining-time latent thoughts).

title: State Stream Transformer (SST) V2: Parallel Training of Nonlinear Recurrence for Latent Space Reasoning
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: SST V2 adds an FFN-driven nonlinear recurrence per decoder layer that streams latent state across positions and allows extra latent deliberation per position; co-trained into a 27B backbone on GSM8K data it beats a fine-tuning-matched baseline.

claims.claim: Co-training the state stream into a 27B backbone on a small GSM8K set gives +15.15 points on GPQA-Diamond over a fine-tuning-matched baseline.
claims.evidence_quote: Co-trained into an existing 27B backbone using only a small dataset of GSM8K examples, the SST delivers a +15.15 point gain over a fine-tuning-matched baseline on out-of-distribution GPQA-Diamond

claims.claim: The same recurrence supports per-position latent deliberation at inference, spending extra FLOPs before committing to a token.
claims.evidence_quote: This same mechanism supports continuous latent deliberation per position at inference time, dedicating additional FLOPs to exploring abstract reasoning before committing to a token.

numbers.what: GPQA-Diamond gain and GSM8K error reduction vs fine-tuning-matched baseline
numbers.quote: the SST delivers a +15.15 point gain over a fine-tuning-matched baseline on out-of-distribution GPQA-Diamond and cuts that same baseline's remaining GSM8K errors by 46%

survey_notes: Hybrid of horizontal state streaming and per-position latent iteration; extra inference compute per token without new tokens, which is close to depth recurrence in effect. Comparisons against 'models up to 25 times larger' are unmatched. Abstract only; full text not read per assignment.

title: Trading Depth for Time in Recurrent Transformers
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: In Latent Recurrent Transformers, one latent thought token through the same L layers between vocabulary tokens recovers 67-81% of the gain of doubling depth to 2L, at equal blocks per vocabulary token and about 48% fewer parameters.

claims.claim: An L-layer LRT with one thought token comes within 0.006/0.004 bits per byte of a 2L-layer LRT, recovering 67%/81% of the improvement with about 48% fewer parameters.
claims.evidence_quote: one thought token brings the shallower model within 0.006 and 0.004 bits per byte of its double-depth counterpart, recovering 67% and 81% of the improvement with approximately 48% fewer total parameters.

claims.claim: The comparison is controlled: both models execute 2L blocks per vocabulary token during decoding; only parameter count differs.
claims.evidence_quote: Both execute $2L$ Transformer blocks per vocabulary token during decoding, but the thought-token model uses fewer parameters.

numbers.what: BPB gap to double-depth model; fraction of improvement recovered; parameter saving
numbers.quote: one thought token brings the shallower model within 0.006 and 0.004 bits per byte of its double-depth counterpart, recovering 67% and 81% of the improvement with approximately 48% fewer total parameters.

survey_notes: Most direct sequence-axis analogue of the looped-model iso-effective-depth regime: time (an extra thought pass through shared weights) substitutes for physical depth at matched blocks per token. Result pattern mirrors looped-model findings: parameter-efficient, but the deeper unshared model still wins at equal compute. Abstract only.

title: Recursive Multi-Agent Systems
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: RecursiveMAS links heterogeneous agents into one latent-space recursive loop via a RecursiveLink module and inner-outer loop training, reporting accuracy gains, speedups and token savings over single/multi-agent and recursive baselines on 9 benchmarks.

claims.claim: The paper frames looped/recursive LMs as a scaling axis and extends recursion from one model to a multi-agent system.
claims.evidence_quote: Recursive or looped language models have recently emerged as a new scaling axis by iteratively refining the same model computation over latent states to deepen reasoning.

claims.claim: Across 9 benchmarks RecursiveMAS improves average accuracy by 8.3% with 1.2x-2.4x speedup and 34.6%-75.6% token reduction vs single/multi-agent and recursive baselines.
claims.evidence_quote: RecursiveMAS consistently delivers an average accuracy improvement of 8.3%, together with 1.2$\times$-2.4$\times$ end-to-end inference speedup, and 34.6%-75.6% token usage reduction.

numbers.what: average accuracy gain; speedup; token reduction
numbers.quote: RecursiveMAS consistently delivers an average accuracy improvement of 8.3%, together with 1.2$\times$-2.4$\times$ end-to-end inference speedup, and 34.6%-75.6% token usage reduction.

builds_on: looped / recursive language models (unspecified in abstract)
survey_notes: Explicitly builds on the looped-LM scaling-axis framing and compares against 'recursive computation baselines' (identity and matching not stated in abstract). Latent state transfer across agents is a sequence/agent-axis recursion, not depth recurrence. Full text exists but was not read per assignment.

title: Recirculation
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Recirculation is a training-free (or lightly tuned) inference-time recurrence for frozen foundation models that lets the model track belief states, positioned explicitly against CoT and depth looping; adaptive recirculation lowers perplexity and raises GSM8k accuracy on Gemma3.

claims.claim: The authors distinguish recirculation from chain-of-thought and from depth-recurrence (looping).
claims.evidence_quote: We distinguish this technique from chain-of-thought computation---which is better reserved for complex inferences rather than basic state tracking---as well as from popular depth-recurrence techniques (looping) and the costly training of recurrent transformers.

claims.claim: Adaptive recirculation on frozen Gemma3 models reduces perplexity and gives a 21% relative GSM8k accuracy increase over the off-the-shelf baseline.
claims.evidence_quote: adaptive recirculation achieves surprising gains on the Gemma3 family, including a consistent reduction in perplexity on a suite of datasets, a 21% increase in relative accuracy on GSM8k

numbers.what: relative GSM8k accuracy increase over off-the-shelf Gemma3
numbers.quote: a 21% increase in relative accuracy on GSM8k, and reliable improvements in accuracy on other downstream tasks

limitations: Requires serial processing in the prefill phase (abstract).
survey_notes: Competing training-free alternative to training-free depth looping of pretrained models; recurrence is over sequence positions (state tracking) with serial prefill. Useful contrast for the retrofit/training-free looping section. Full text exists, not read per assignment.

title: Emergent Search and Backtracking in Latent Reasoning Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Decoding the evolving beliefs of a latent reasoning transformer step by step on multiple-choice QA shows structured latent search: exploration, tentative commitment, and frequent, beneficial backtracking.

claims.claim: Backtracking in latent deliberation occurs in 32% of instances and is associated with a 34% accuracy gain over non-backtracking instances.
claims.evidence_quote: Backtracking is prevalent (32% of instances), beneficial (34% accuracy gain over non-backtracking instances), and predominantly directed away from the semantically closest distractor toward the correct answer.

claims.claim: Latent search is adaptive: implausible distractors shorten exploration by 54%.
claims.evidence_quote: The search is adaptive: replacing distractors with implausible alternatives shortens exploration by 54%.

numbers.what: share of instances with backtracking; accuracy gain
numbers.quote: Backtracking is prevalent (32% of instances), beneficial (34% accuracy gain over non-backtracking instances)

numbers.what: reduction in exploration length with implausible distractors
numbers.quote: The search is adaptive: replacing distractors with implausible alternatives shortens exploration by 54%.

survey_notes: The abstract does not name the latent reasoning transformer studied; if it is a depth-recurrent model (lead author should check the full text), this belongs in the mechanisms section as evidence of iterative search across loops. Conceptually parallels Coconut's BFS claim (2412.06769).

title: Temporal Recurrence Favors Fewer Layers
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: A compute-allocation study over within-step depth, expert width and parallel experts finds that, at approximately matched per-step compute, temporally recurrent models prefer substantially fewer layers with comparable or better performance (Sokoban, FineWeb LM).

claims.claim: Temporal recurrence shifts the best compute allocation toward substantially fewer layers per step with comparable or better performance.
claims.evidence_quote: Across Sokoban and autoregressive FineWeb language modeling, we find that temporal recurrence shifts the best observed compute allocation toward substantially fewer layers, with comparable or better performance.

claims.claim: The comparison is between best observed recurrent and non-recurrent allocations under approximately matched per-step computation across budgets.
claims.evidence_quote: For each budget, we compare the best observed recurrent and non-recurrent allocations and the performance they achieve under approximately matched per-step computation.

survey_notes: Complements 2609.21605 and 2604.21215: carrying latent state across time substitutes for within-step depth. For the survey: evidence that depth and temporal recurrence are partially interchangeable, which bears on whether looping depth and sequence-axis recurrence should be combined. Abstract only.

title: Not All Thinking is Created Equal: Latent Reasoning Discovers a Recurrent Search Algorithm for Depth Generalization
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Five variants of one GPTNeoX backbone trained from scratch on ProsQA-Ext show vanilla, CoT and pause-token models fit in-distribution but fail on longer hops, while end-to-end latent-reasoning models learn a reusable recurrent reachability-search circuit that generalizes beyond training depth.

claims.claim: Vanilla, CoT and pause-token models do well in distribution but generalize poorly to longer-hop OOD problems.
claims.evidence_quote: Vanilla, CoT, and Pause Token models solve ID problems well, but rely largely on local graph features and generalize poorly to out-of-distribution (OOD) problems with longer hops.

claims.claim: Latent recurrence learns a reusable forward-search algorithm that generalizes beyond the training depth.
claims.evidence_quote: In this setting, latent recurrence supports a reusable forward-search algorithm that generalizes beyond the training depth.

claims.claim: Circuit analysis localizes a sparse recurrent search circuit: an attention head retrieves relations and the MLP/residual update the reachability state across recurrent steps.
claims.evidence_quote: an attention head retrieves graph relations, an MLP and the residual stream update the reachability state across recurrent steps, while multiple attention heads together then do the candidate matching.

survey_notes: Direct head-to-head of thinking mechanisms on one backbone and data (iso-param, iso-data; inference compute differs). title: Hidden Decoding at Scale: Latent Computation Scaling for Large Language Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Hidden Decoding expands each token into n streams with separate embeddings during continued pretraining, keeping intermediate streams' KV cache, with stream-factorized attention; trained at 80B and 617B MoE scale it improves matched non-HD baselines, positioned as a pipeline-parallel-friendly alternative to looping.

claims.claim: The authors argue looped Transformers are hard to scale because looped computation conflicts with pipeline parallelism, motivating sequence-length scaling instead.
claims.evidence_quote: Depth-recurrent (looped) Transformers pursue this goal but are hard to scale, because looped computation does not fit naturally with the pipeline parallelism used to train the largest models.

claims.claim: WeLM-HD4-80B and WeLM-HD4-617B (n=4) improve their matched non-HD baselines, the first sequence-length scaling demonstration at 100B+ MoE scale.
claims.evidence_quote: At frontier scale, we train WeLM-HD4-80B and WeLM-HD4-617B at n=4 and improve their matched non-HD baselines, making Hidden Decoding the first demonstrated sequence-length scaling method at the 100B+ MoE scale.

claims.claim: Gains grow with the expansion factor n.
claims.evidence_quote: Across expansion factors, the gains grow as n increases, showing that sequence-length expansion is a practical fixed-backbone scaling path for frontier-scale LLMs.

numbers.what: model scales trained with n=4
numbers.quote: At frontier scale, we train WeLM-HD4-80B and WeLM-HD4-617B at n=4 and improve their matched non-HD baselines

survey_notes: Key 'competing' paper: explicitly argues against looping on systems grounds (pipeline parallelism) and spends extra per-token compute on the sequence axis instead; KV cache grows with n because intermediate streams are kept. Largest-scale evidence in this group. Matching criterion of 'matched non-HD baselines' not specified in abstract. Full text exists, not read per assignment.

title: N-vium: Mixture-of-Exits Transformer for Accelerated Exact Generation
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (adaptive_depth_without_sharing); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: N-vium attaches prediction heads at several depths and defines the next-token distribution as a learned mixture over exits with token-adaptive routing, deferring upper-layer compute to keep exact sampling and full KV caches; at 1.5B it is 57.9% faster than a matched Transformer at no perplexity cost.

claims.claim: The largest N-vium model achieves a 57.9% wall-clock speedup over a parameter- and data-matched Transformer without perplexity loss.
claims.evidence_quote: Our largest model reaches 57.9% wall-clock speedup over a parameter- and data-matched standard transformer at no perplexity cost.

claims.claim: The mixture-of-exits formulation strictly generalizes the standard Transformer.
claims.evidence_quote: This formulation strictly generalizes the standard transformer, which is recovered exactly when routing assigns zero mass to all intermediate heads.

numbers.what: wall-clock speedup at 1.5B over matched transformer
numbers.quote: Our largest model reaches 57.9% wall-clock speedup over a parameter- and data-matched standard transformer at no perplexity cost.

survey_notes: Early exit without sharing that solves the KV-cache problem by deferring and batching upper-layer computation; the same trick is relevant to early exit in looped models. Abstract only.

title: The Illusion of Superposition? A Principled Analysis of Latent Thinking in Language Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Probing latent CoT in training-free, fine-tuned and from-scratch regimes finds superposition only in models trained from scratch; in training-free and fine-tuned regimes it collapses or is unused, attributed to natural-language pretraining and capacity.

claims.claim: In training-free and fine-tuned latent-CoT regimes superposition collapses or is unused, and models find shortcuts.
claims.evidence_quote: In the training-free and fine-tuned regimes, we find that the superposition either collapses or is not used at all, with models discovering shortcut solutions instead.

claims.claim: Two causes are proposed: language pretraining biases late layers to commit to a token, and capacity shapes which solution is favored.
claims.evidence_quote: i) pretraining on natural language data biases models to commit to a token in the last layers ii) capacity has a huge effect on which solutions a model favors

survey_notes: Contradiction to record: Coconut (2412.06769) reports BFS-like superposition after fine-tuning a pretrained GPT-2, and 2505.12514/2509.23365 show it can emerge in training; this paper finds superposition only from scratch. title: Inverse Depth Scaling From Most Layers Being Similar
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Analysis of LLMs and toy residual networks finds loss scales inversely with depth, attributed to functionally similar layers averaging errors like an ensemble rather than compositional computation.

claims.claim: Loss scales inversely proportional to depth, probably because functionally similar layers reduce error by ensemble averaging.
claims.evidence_quote: We find loss scales inversely proportional to depth in LLMs, probably due to functionally similar layers reducing error through ensemble averaging rather than compositional learning or discretizing smooth dynamics.

claims.evidence_quote: The findings suggest that improving LLM efficiency may require architectural innovations to encourage compositional use of depth.

survey_notes: Agrees with 2505.13898 and 2512.14064 that standard depth is used non-compositionally. If most layers are functionally similar, this is indirect support for sharing them (looping); the survey should present that as an inference, not the paper's claim. Abstract only.

title: Full-bandwidth transformer

claims.claim: Latent feedback lets 1B models match or approach standard Transformers trained with about 1.5x more tokens, with negligible decoding overhead.
claims.evidence_quote: With negligible per-token decoding overhead, full-bandwidth transformers match or approach standard transformers trained with roughly 1.5x more tokens, and manage to produce shorter reasoning when no off-policy templates are provided.

claims.claim: Mechanism: the previous top-layer hidden state is fused with the sampled token embedding via a gated linear unit and fed back as input.
claims.evidence_quote: at each decoding step, the previous top-layer hidden state is fused with the sampled token embedding through a gated linear unit and fed back as the next input.

numbers.what: model size and max training tokens
numbers.quote: We train 1B-parameter full-bandwidth transformers on up to 400B tokens

numbers.what: token-efficiency equivalent
numbers.quote: match or approach standard transformers trained with roughly 1.5x more tokens

title: Do Transformers Use their Depth Adaptively? Evidence from a Relational Reasoning Task

relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model

claims.evidence_quote: On 150M and 300M parameter C4 pretraining, Recurrent Transformers improve cross-entropy over a parameter-matched Transformer baseline and achieve the improvement with fewer layers (fixed parameters)

claims.evidence_quote: a simple architectural change where each layer attends to key-value pairs computed off its own activations, yielding layerwise recurrent memory while preserving standard autoregressive decoding cost.

numbers.what: pretraining scales

title: Physics of Language Models: Part 3.3, Knowledge Capacity Scaling Laws
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (theory_scaling_and_depth_growth_background); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Controlled experiments estimate that language models store about 2 bits of factual knowledge per parameter (even at int8) and study how training duration, architecture, quantization, MoE and data noise affect capacity.

claims.claim: Language models can store only about 2 bits of knowledge per parameter, even when quantized to int8.
claims.evidence_quote: we establish that language models can and only can store 2 bits of knowledge per parameter, even when quantized to int8, and such knowledge can be flexibly extracted for downstream applications.

numbers.what: knowledge capacity per parameter
numbers.quote: language models can and only can store 2 bits of knowledge per parameter, even when quantized to int8

survey_notes: Background for the parameters-vs-compute split: if knowledge capacity scales with unique parameters, looping (more compute, same parameters) should help reasoning more than memorization. Looped-model papers that report this split (knowledge vs reasoning) can be framed against this. Abstract only.

title: Do Large Language Models Latently Perform Multi-Hop Reasoning?
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Tests whether LLMs latently resolve a bridge entity and then use it; finds strong first-hop evidence for some relation types, moderate second-hop evidence, and size scaling for the first hop only.

claims.claim: For certain relation types, the latent multi-hop pathway is used in more than 80% of prompts.
claims.evidence_quote: We find strong evidence of latent multi-hop reasoning for the prompts of certain relation types, with the reasoning pathway used in more than 80% of the prompts.

claims.claim: Model size scaling improves the first hop but not the second.
claims.evidence_quote: we find a clear scaling trend with increasing model size for the first hop of reasoning but not for the second hop.

numbers.what: share of prompts using latent pathway for some relation types
numbers.quote: with the reasoning pathway used in more than 80% of the prompts

survey_notes: Evidence that stacked depth composes poorly beyond one hop, consistent with 2505.13898 and 2505.17923; motivates more serial depth (looping) for multi-hop. Abstract only.

title: Physics of Language Models: Part 2.1, Grade-School Math and the Hidden Reasoning Process
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Controlled synthetic grade-school-math experiments probe whether LMs truly reason, what hidden reasoning process they use, and how large or deep a model must be.

claims.claim: The study addresses, among other questions, how large or deep a model must be to solve GSM8K-level problems.
claims.evidence_quote: (6) How large or deep must a model be to effectively solve GSM8K-level math questions?

survey_notes: Abstract poses the depth question but states no answer; the depth finding must be taken from the full text (not available here). Abstract only.

title: Transformers, parallel computation, and logarithmic depth
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (theory_scaling_and_depth_growth_background); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Shows constant numbers of self-attention layers and Massively Parallel Computation rounds simulate each other, so logarithmic depth suffices for tasks other sequence models and sub-quadratic approximations cannot solve efficiently.

claims.claim: Logarithmic depth suffices for Transformers to solve basic tasks that other sequence models cannot solve efficiently.
claims.evidence_quote: we show that logarithmic depth is sufficient for transformers to solve basic computational tasks that cannot be efficiently solved by several other neural sequence models and sub-quadratic transformer approximations.

survey_notes: Theory background on depth ~ parallel rounds; looped models realize log-depth with constant parameters. Abstract only.

title: Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners: A Mechanistic Journey to the Edge of Generalization
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Transformers learn implicit composition and comparison over parametric knowledge only via grokking; composition fails to generalize OOD while comparison succeeds, and circuit analysis suggests cross-layer knowledge sharing as an architectural fix.

claims.claim: Out of distribution, transformers fail to generalize systematically for composition but succeed for comparison.
claims.evidence_quote: when faced with out-of-distribution examples, transformers fail to systematically generalize for composition but succeed for comparison.

claims.claim: The authors suggest architectural changes such as encouraging cross-layer knowledge sharing.
claims.evidence_quote: Our findings guide data and training setup to better induce implicit reasoning and suggest potential improvements to the transformer architecture, such as encouraging cross-layer knowledge sharing.

survey_notes: Widely cited motivation for weight sharing across layers (looping): composition fails because second-hop knowledge must be stored in later layers. Duplicate corpus entry exists with arxiv_id null (title 'Grokking of Implicit Reasoning in Transformers...'). Abstract only.

title: SOLAR 10.7B: Scaling Large Language Models with Simple yet Effective Depth Up-Scaling
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (theory_scaling_and_depth_growth_background); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Depth up-scaling (DUS) grows a smaller LLM by depthwise layer duplication plus continued pretraining, producing SOLAR 10.7B; the instruct variant is reported to surpass Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct.

claims.claim: DUS scales LLMs through depthwise scaling plus continued pretraining, without MoE-style changes.
claims.evidence_quote: we present a method for scaling LLMs called depth up-scaling (DUS), which encompasses depthwise scaling and continued pretraining.

claims.claim: SOLAR 10.7B-Instruct is reported to surpass Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct.
claims.evidence_quote: Building on the DUS model, we additionally present SOLAR 10.7B-Instruct, a variant fine-tuned for instruction-following capabilities, surpassing Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct.

numbers.what: model size
numbers.quote: We introduce SOLAR 10.7B, a large language model (LLM) with 10.7 billion parameters

survey_notes: Untied counterpart of retrofit looping: duplicate layers then untie and continue pretraining. Useful contrast for retrofit-from-dense looped models (which keep duplicated layers tied). Comparison to Mixtral is unmatched. Abstract only.

title: Think before you speak: Training Language Models With Pause Tokens
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Pause-training appends learnable pause tokens so the model processes extra hidden vectors before answering; gains appear when models are both pretrained and finetuned with pauses (1B and 130M decoders on C4).

claims.claim: Inference-time delays help only when the model is both pretrained and finetuned with them.
claims.evidence_quote: Our main finding is that inference-time delays show gains when the model is both pre-trained and finetuned with delays.

claims.claim: At 1B, pause-training improves 8 of 9 tasks, including +18% EM on SQuAD, +8% on CommonSenseQA and +1% on GSM8k.
claims.evidence_quote: For the 1B model, we witness gains on 8 of 9 tasks, most prominently, a gain of $18\%$ EM score on the QA task of SQuAD, $8\%$ on CommonSenseQA and $1\%$ accuracy on the reasoning task of GSM8k.

numbers.what: gains of 1B pause-trained model
numbers.quote: For the 1B model, we witness gains on 8 of 9 tasks, most prominently, a gain of $18\%$ EM score on the QA task of SQuAD, $8\%$ on CommonSenseQA and $1\%$ accuracy on the reasoning task of GSM8k.

survey_notes: Canonical 'extra positions, no extra depth' baseline. Same-architecture comparison (iso-param); inference FLOPs differ. Pause tokens add parallel width per token rather than serial depth (see theory in 2505.21024). In 2412.06769 Table 1 pause tokens underperform Coconut on GSM8k. Abstract only.

title: Transformers learn to implement preconditioned gradient descent for in-context learning
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (theory_scaling_and_depth_growth_background); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Loss-landscape analysis of linear Transformers on random linear regression: the one-layer global minimum implements one step of preconditioned gradient descent, and L-layer critical points implement L steps.

claims.claim: For L attention layers, certain critical points implement L iterations of preconditioned gradient descent.
claims.evidence_quote: For a transformer with $L$ attention layers, we prove certain critical points of the training objective implement $L$ iterations of preconditioned gradient descent.

survey_notes: Layers-as-optimizer-steps view that underlies looped-transformer ICL theory (one shared layer iterated = repeated GD steps). Abstract only.

title: Test like you Train in Implicit Deep Learning
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (deep_equilibrium_and_implicit); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Theory and experiments show that for overparametrized implicit models, running more inner iterations at test time than in training does not improve performance; DEQs do not benefit while meta-learning does.

claims.claim: For overparametrized networks, increasing test-time iterations cannot improve performance.
claims.evidence_quote: We demonstrate that overparametrization plays a key role: increasing the number of iterations at test time cannot improve performance for overparametrized networks.

claims.claim: DEQs, typically overparametrized, do not benefit from more inference iterations, while meta-learning does.
claims.evidence_quote: DEQs, which are typically overparametrized, do not benefit from increasing the number of iterations at inference while meta-learning, which is typically not overparametrized, benefits from it.

survey_notes: Important counterpoint for the survey's test-time loop extrapolation section: 'more iterations at test time' is not free improvement for overparametrized implicit models. Contrasts with looped/recurrent claims of extrapolation by adding loops (as summarized in 2507.06203 Sec. 3.1.5) and with path-independence arguments (2211.09961, in corpus). Abstract only.

title: EE-LLM: Large-Scale Training and Inference of Early-Exit Large Language Models with 3D Parallelism
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (adaptive_depth_without_sharing); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: EE-LLM is a Megatron-LM-based framework for training and serving early-exit LLMs with 3D parallelism, including pipeline-compatible backpropagation for exit losses and KV-cache-compatible early-exit inference.

claims.claim: EE-LLM trains early-exit LLMs with negligible overhead and gives inference speedups without quality loss.
claims.evidence_quote: EE-LLM achieves great training efficiency with negligible computational overhead compared to standard LLM training, as well as outstanding inference speedup without compromising output quality.

claims.claim: It provides two early-exit inference methods compatible with KV caching.
claims.evidence_quote: two approaches of early-exit inference that are compatible with KV caching for autoregressive generation.

survey_notes: Systems reference for early exit at scale with pipeline parallelism, the setting Hidden Decoding (2607.08186) says is hard for looping. KV-cache handling for skipped layers is a shared problem with exit-in-loop models. Abstract only.

title: Transformers Learn Shortcuts to Automata
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (theory_scaling_and_depth_growth_background); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Shallow Transformers can exactly simulate finite-state automata on length-T inputs with o(T) layers via hierarchical reparameterization (O(log T) always, O(1) often), these shortcuts are learnable, but they are brittle.

claims.claim: Transformers with o(T) layers can exactly replicate an automaton on length-T sequences (shortcut solutions).
claims.evidence_quote: Our theoretical results characterize shortcut solutions, whereby a Transformer with $o(T)$ layers can exactly replicate the computation of an automaton on an input sequence of length $T$.

claims.claim: Shortcut solutions are learnable but brittle.
claims.evidence_quote: We further investigate the brittleness of these solutions and propose potential mitigations.

survey_notes: Key contrast for length generalization: non-recurrent shallow models learn brittle parallel shortcuts, while looped models are argued to learn iterative (recurrent) solutions that extrapolate. Abstract only.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Few-shot chain-of-thought exemplars make sufficiently large LMs produce intermediate reasoning steps, improving arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning; a 540B model reaches state-of-the-art GSM8K.

claims.claim: Prompting a 540B model with eight CoT exemplars achieves state-of-the-art GSM8K accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: prompting a 540B-parameter language model with just eight chain of thought exemplars achieves state of the art accuracy on the GSM8K benchmark of math word problems

survey_notes: Token-axis test-time compute baseline against which latent and looped methods are compared. Abstract only.

title: Scalable Adaptive Computation for Iterative Generation
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (diffusion_and_iterative_refinement); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Recurrent Interface Networks route most compute to a small set of latent tokens via cross-attention, and carry latent tokens across reverse-diffusion steps (latent self-conditioning), giving efficient pixel diffusion for images and video.

claims.claim: Latent tokens at each reverse-diffusion forward pass are conditioned on those from prior computation (latent self-conditioning).
claims.evidence_quote: We show how to leverage recurrence by conditioning the latent tokens at each forward pass of the reverse diffusion process with those from prior computation, i.e. latent self-conditioning.

claims.claim: RINs reach state-of-the-art pixel diffusion and are up to 10X more efficient than 2D and 3D U-Nets.
claims.evidence_quote: RINs yield state-of-the-art pixel diffusion models for image and video generation, scaling to 1024X1024 images without cascades or guidance, while being domain-agnostic and up to 10X more efficient than 2D and 3D U-Nets.

numbers.what: efficiency vs U-Nets; max resolution
numbers.quote: scaling to 1024X1024 images without cascades or guidance, while being domain-agnostic and up to 10X more efficient than 2D and 3D U-Nets

survey_notes: Diffusion-step recurrence that carries a latent state between denoising passes, the same idea later applied to DLMs (Relay 2605.22967). Bridges family (b) and looping: each denoising step is a pass of shared weights with carried state. Abstract only.

title: Attention is Not All You Need: Pure Attention Loses Rank Doubly Exponentially with Depth
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Decomposing self-attention networks into paths shows pure attention (no skips or MLPs) converges doubly exponentially to rank 1 with depth; skip connections and MLPs prevent this.

claims.claim: Without skip connections or MLPs, self-attention output converges doubly exponentially to a rank-1 matrix with depth.
claims.evidence_quote: without skip connections or multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), the output converges doubly exponentially to a rank-1 matrix.

claims.claim: Skip connections and MLPs stop the degeneration.
claims.evidence_quote: On the other hand, skip connections and MLPs stop the output from degeneration.

survey_notes: Relevant to many-loop stability: repeatedly applying shared attention risks token-uniformity collapse; residuals/MLPs (and input injection in looped models) counteract it. Abstract only.

title: Perceiver: General Perception with Iterative Attention

claims.claim: Asymmetric attention iteratively distills inputs into a tight latent bottleneck, scaling to very large inputs.
claims.evidence_quote: The model leverages an asymmetric attention mechanism to iteratively distill inputs into a tight latent bottleneck, allowing it to scale to handle very large inputs.

claims.claim: Perceiver is comparable to ResNet-50 and ViT on ImageNet by attending to 50,000 pixels without 2D convolutions.
claims.evidence_quote: The Perceiver obtains performance comparable to ResNet-50 and ViT on ImageNet without 2D convolutions by directly attending to 50,000 pixels.

survey_notes: Iterative latent-bottleneck refinement; weight sharing across iterations is not stated in the abstract (check full text before citing it as a looped model). Abstract only.

title: Multiscale Deep Equilibrium Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (deep_equilibrium_and_implicit); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: MDEQ solves for and backpropagates through equilibria at multiple resolutions simultaneously with implicit differentiation (O(1) memory), matching competitive vision models on ImageNet and Cityscapes.

claims.claim: MDEQ uses implicit differentiation to avoid storing intermediate states, needing only O(1) memory.
claims.evidence_quote: An MDEQ directly solves for and backpropagates through the equilibrium points of multiple feature resolutions simultaneously, using implicit differentiation to avoid storing intermediate states (and thus requiring only $O(1)$ memory consumption).

claims.claim: MDEQs match or exceed competitive vision models on ImageNet and Cityscapes, a first for implicit models at that scale.
claims.evidence_quote: MDEQs are able to match or exceed the performance of recent competitive computer vision models: the first time such performance and scale have been achieved by an implicit deep learning approach.

survey_notes: Implicit-model reference for constant training memory via implicit gradients (vs BPTT memory growth in looped models). Abstract only.

title: Monotone operator equilibrium networks

title: Ceiling of a Task: When Can a Transformer Succeed Without Its Chain of Thought?
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Treating a fixed-depth Transformer pass as a shallow circuit, the paper defines a task's ceiling (best shallow-circuit accuracy) and proves chain content is necessary on serial tasks; experiments on finite-group word problems and MATH-500/AIME confirm erasing the chain collapses accuracy.

claims.claim: Any procedure that runs a fixed-depth model a constant number of times is still a shallow circuit.
claims.evidence_quote: One forward pass through a fixed number of layers has constant depth, so any procedure that runs the model a constant number of times is a shallow circuit.

claims.claim: On MATH-500 and AIME, erasing the chain costs open reasoning models 0.52-0.82 accuracy, sentence shuffles are harmless and token shuffles as harmful as erasure.
claims.evidence_quote: On MATH-500 and AIME, erasing the chain costs open reasoning models 0.52 to 0.82 accuracy, a sentence shuffle is harmless, and a token shuffle is as harmful as erasing

claims.claim: Replacing the chain with content-independent filler drives accuracy down to the ceiling (chance on maximally serial tasks).
claims.evidence_quote: replacing the chain by anything that does not depend on its content, such as filler tokens or a restatement of the question, drives the accuracy down to the ceiling, and on a maximally serial task down to chance.

numbers.what: accuracy lost when erasing the chain on MATH-500/AIME
numbers.quote: erasing the chain costs open reasoning models 0.52 to 0.82 accuracy

survey_notes: Implication for looped models (my inference, not the paper's claim): a constant number of loops keeps the model a shallow circuit, so loops must grow with input size to escape the ceiling on serial tasks, matching 2503.03961. Also contradicts the idea that pause/filler tokens substitute for CoT on serial tasks (cf. 2404.15758, which shows filler helps only on specific parallelizable tasks). Abstract only.

title: Demystifying Hidden-State Recurrence: Switchable Latent Reasoning with On-Policy Reinforcement Learning

claims.claim: Discrete entry/exit tokens make the GRPO policy ratio well-defined for latent reasoning.
claims.evidence_quote: Because the boundaries are ordinary discrete tokens, the GRPO policy ratio is well-defined at every decision point.

claims.claim: SWITCH outperforms prior hidden-state-recurrence latent reasoning methods at similar scale.
claims.evidence_quote: SWITCH consistently outperforms prior hidden-state-recurrence latent reasoning approaches at similar scale.

claims.claim: The latent computation is concentrated at a single hidden-state transition on entry.
claims.evidence_quote: that computation is concentrated at a single hidden-state transition on entry.

title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: LIFT feeds a predicted information-dense state back across generation steps; during pretraining the input state is precomputed from an off-the-shelf LM's next-token distribution, keeping training fully parallel; 135M-1B models beat token-matched Transformers.

claims.claim: Teacher-provided states make recurrent-state pretraining fully parallel across positions.
claims.evidence_quote: As the input states are precomputed, pretraining remains fully parallel across positions.

claims.claim: From 135M to 1B, LIFT beats standard Transformers at a token-matched budget and is on par with or ahead of compute-matched Transformers.
claims.evidence_quote: Experiments with pretrained models ranging from 135M to 1B parameters show that LIFT consistently outperforms standard Transformers and baselines on language modeling, downstream reasoning tasks, and procedural tasks under token-matched budget, while being on par with or ahead of compute-matched Transformers.

claims.claim: On a state-tracking task, a tiny LIFT beats same-size Transformers trained on 8x more data.
claims.evidence_quote: a controlled study on a state-tracking task shows that a tiny LIFT outperforms same-size Transformers trained on 8x more data, even when trained with the states of a Transformer that fails the task.

claims.evidence_quote: We compare CoT models against a same-depth no-CoT baseline, a deeper baseline matched to the CoT model in effective depth, and a looped transformer with weight-tied recurrence but no additional chain-of-thought tokens.

title: The Depth Ceiling: On the Limits of Large Language Models in Discovering Latent Planning
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: On graph path-finding with controlled latent planning depth, models trained only on final answers discover strategies of at most 3 (tiny from-scratch) to 5 (fine-tuned GPT-4o, Qwen3-32B) latent steps, though discovered strategies execute up to 8 steps at test time.

claims.claim: Discoverable latent planning depth is small: 3 steps for tiny from-scratch transformers, 5 for fine-tuned GPT-4o/Qwen3-32B, 7 for GPT-5.4 few-shot.
claims.evidence_quote: tiny transformers trained from scratch discover strategies requiring up to three latent steps, fine-tuned GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B reach five, and GPT-5.4 attains seven under few-shot prompting.

claims.claim: Strategies learned up to 5 steps generalize up to 8 steps at test time, dissociating discovery from execution.
claims.evidence_quote: Although the maximum latent planning depth models can learn during training is five, the discovered strategy generalizes up to eight latent steps at test-time.

title: Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: REST adds four differentiable representation losses (causality, minimality, separability, stability) to cross-entropy for latent thoughts in recurrent single-agent and multi-agent systems, improving accuracy at equal data, compute and latent budget.

claims.claim: CE-only training of latent thoughts has failure modes such as collapsing thoughts across questions and retaining irrelevant information.
claims.evidence_quote: Theoretical and empirical analyses establish and confirm four failures of CE-only training that lead to a lower probability of the correct answer such as collapsing thoughts across distinct questions and retaining irrelevant information.

claims.claim: At equal data, compute and latent budget, REST improves accuracy by up to 7.5 points and convergence by 30%.
claims.evidence_quote: with the same training data, compute, and latent budget, REST increases accuracy over CE-only training across agent settings and model sizes by up to 7.5 percentage points and convergence on a final answer by 30\%.

numbers.what: max accuracy gain over CE-only; convergence gain
numbers.quote: REST increases accuracy over CE-only training across agent settings and model sizes by up to 7.5 percentage points and convergence on a final answer by 30\%.

survey_notes: Thought-collapse diagnosis parallels SIM-CoT (2509.20317). Applies to systems 'recurring on their own hidden states'; the losses could transfer to per-loop states of looped models. Abstract only.

title: Learned Relay Representations for Forward-Thinking Discrete Diffusion Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (diffusion_and_iterative_refinement); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Relay adds a differentiable per-token channel that carries latent information between masked-diffusion denoising passes, trained with truncated BPTT; on Fast-dLLM v2 it beats standard SFT on coding while cutting latency up to 32%.

claims.claim: Relay passes latent information between forward passes through a per-token channel trained by truncated BPTT.
claims.evidence_quote: Relay introduces a differentiable per-token channel that passes information between forward passes and is trained via truncated backpropagation through time (BPTT).

claims.claim: On Fast-dLLM v2, Relay outperforms standard SFT on coding while reducing latency by up to 32%.
claims.evidence_quote: We then scale Relay to Fast-dLLM v2, a state-of-the-art DLM, outperforming standard supervised finetuning on coding tasks while reducing inference latency by up to 32%.

numbers.what: inference latency reduction
numbers.quote: outperforming standard supervised finetuning on coding tasks while reducing inference latency by up to 32%.

survey_notes: Turns diffusion denoising into a recurrent latent loop (state carried across passes), making DLMs structurally close to looped models with input injection; same truncated-BPTT trade-off as looped training. Abstract only.

title: LLM Reasoning Is Latent, Not the Chain of Thought

claims.evidence_quote: H0, most apparent reasoning gains are better explained by generic serial compute than by any privileged representational object.

claims.claim: Current evidence most strongly supports H1 (latent-state trajectories) as a default working hypothesis.
claims.evidence_quote: we find that current evidence most strongly supports H1 as a default working hypothesis rather than as a task-independent verdict.

claims.claim: Evaluations should disentangle surface traces, latent states and serial compute.
claims.evidence_quote: it should evaluate reasoning with designs that explicitly disentangle surface traces, latent states, and serial compute.

survey_notes: Methodological ally of our regime audit: matched serial-compute budgets are needed to separate representation from compute (H0). Looped models are a clean way to add serial compute without surface tokens. Abstract only.

title: Latent Reasoning with Supervised Thinking States

claims.evidence_quote: Thinking States generates sequences of thinking tokens every few input tokens, transforms the thoughts back into embedding space, and adds them to the following input tokens.

claims.claim: Because thoughts are tokens, they can be supervised with natural language and trained by parallel teacher forcing.
claims.evidence_quote: since the thoughts are represented as tokens, they can be learned from natural language supervision, and using teacher-forcing, which is parallelizable.

survey_notes: Interleaves recurrence with input processing (reasoning during prefill), a different placement of extra compute than looping or Coconut. Abstract only.

title: T^2MLR: Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: T2MLR fuses a cached middle-layer representation of the previous token into an earlier layer of the current token, giving cross-time latent recurrence at low inference cost; it beats data- and parameter-matched baselines and middle-block recurrence beats full-layer recurrence.

claims.evidence_quote: Across natural-language pretraining and multi-hop reasoning finetuning, T2MLR consistently outperforms data- and parameter-matched Transformer base lines.

claims.claim: Recurring through only a localized middle-layer block (as little as 20% of the network) often beats full-layer recurrence.
claims.evidence_quote: applying recurrence to only a localized middle-layer block (as little as 20% of the network) often outperforms full-layer recurrence.

claims.claim: The authors conclude effective latent reasoning does not require looping over all layers.
claims.evidence_quote: These results suggest that effective latent reasoning in Transformers does not require looping over all layers as in previous works, but can instead emerge more strongly from targeted middle-layer recurrence.

numbers.what: fraction of network in recurrent block that can suffice
numbers.quote: applying recurrence to only a localized middle-layer block (as little as 20% of the network) often outperforms full-layer recurrence.

survey_notes: Directly speaks to looped-model design: partial (middle-block) recurrence beats whole-stack recurrence, consistent with sandwich/prelude-core-coda findings in looped models, but here the recurrence is across time (previous token) rather than within a token. claims.evidence_quote: This work explores an alternative axis: increasing per-token computation without expanding parameters, by internalizing latent Chain-of-Thought (CoT) into pretraining.

title: Forward-Free Diffusion Language Models with BPTT-Free Looped Refinement
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (diffusion_and_iterative_refinement); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: FReDA drops the hand-designed forward corruption process: model-generated drafts serve as intermediate states and a refinement model is trained by backpropagating only through the final refinement pass; FReDA-4B beats larger diffusion base models on reasoning and coding.

claims.claim: Training detaches earlier refinement passes and backpropagates only through the last pass, avoiding BPTT.
claims.evidence_quote: Training detaches the preceding refinement passes and backpropagates only through the final pass, avoiding backpropagation through time (BPTT) across refinement iterations while retaining standard backpropagation within the final Transformer pass.

claims.claim: FReDA-4B outperforms larger diffusion base models with up to 15% absolute gains and 1.5-1.8x speedup.
claims.evidence_quote: FReDA-4B outperforms larger diffusion base models on reasoning and coding benchmarks, achieving absolute gains of up to 15%, while reaching a 1.5-1.8x average speedup over diffusion baselines and scaling effectively with additional refinement computation.

numbers.what: max absolute gain; speedup over diffusion baselines
numbers.quote: achieving absolute gains of up to 15%, while reaching a 1.5-1.8x average speedup over diffusion baselines

survey_notes: Looped refinement in output space with last-pass-only gradients: the diffusion analogue of one-step / last-step gradient training in looped and recursive-reasoning models. Comparison against larger models is unmatched. Abstract only.

title: Turbo Connection: Reasoning as Information Flow from Higher to Lower Layers
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: TurboConn routes dense residual connections from higher-layer states of token t to lower layers of token t+1, lifting the fixed-depth limit on latent computation paths; fine-tuned into pretrained LLMs it improves GSM8K, Parity and arithmetic, e.g. Qwen-3-1.7B Parity from 53.78% to 100%.

claims.claim: Multiple residual connections route higher-layer states of token t into lower layers of token t+1.
claims.evidence_quote: routing multiple residual connections from the higher-layer hidden states of each token $t$ to the lower layers of token $t+1$.

claims.claim: Adding TurboConn to a fine-tuned Qwen-3-1.7B raises Parity from 53.78% to 100%.
claims.evidence_quote: while a fine-tuned Qwen-3-1.7B achieves only 53.78% on Parity, adding our architectural modification enables the model to reach 100% accuracy

numbers.what: Parity accuracy of fine-tuned Qwen-3-1.7B without vs with TurboConn
numbers.quote: while a fine-tuned Qwen-3-1.7B achieves only 53.78% on Parity, adding our architectural modification enables the model to reach 100% accuracy

title: Parallel Scaling Law for Language Models

claims.evidence_quote: We introduce the third and more inference-efficient scaling paradigm: increasing the model's parallel computation during both training and inference time.

claims.claim: P parallel streams behave like scaling parameters by O(log P).
claims.evidence_quote: a model with $P$ parallel streams is similar to scaling the parameters by $O(\log P)$ while showing superior inference efficiency.

numbers.quote: ParScale can use up to 22$\times$ less memory increase and 6$\times$ less latency increase compared to parameter scaling

title: Soft Tokens, Hard Truths

title: The Serial Scaling Hypothesis

title: Catch Your Breath: Adaptive Computation for Self-Paced Sequence Production
